title: Beyond Factual Accuracy: Evaluating Coverage of Diverse Factual Information in Long-form Text Generation
abstract: Introduces ICAT for evaluating whether long-form generation covers diverse expected factual information, using atomic-claim decomposition, retrieval-based verification, and alignment of generated claims to expected aspects.

title: Fact in Fragments: Deconstructing Complex Claims via LLM-based Atomic Fact Extraction and Verification
abstract: Presents a framework that iteratively decomposes complex claims into atomic facts, retrieves and reranks evidence, and verifies the resulting facts, including cases where support is fragmented across evidence.

title: Investigating Factuality in Long-Form Text Generation: The Roles of Self-Known and Self-Unknown
abstract: Studies factuality at the atomic-claim level in long-form generation and examines whether models can distinguish claims they know from claims they do not know, connecting claim support with uncertainty behavior.

title: Atomic Contrastive Verification: Fine-Grained Fact-Checking via Claim Decomposition and Knowledge Graph-Grounded Contrastive Reasoning
abstract: Decomposes text into atomic claims and applies knowledge-graph-grounded contrastive reasoning for fine-grained verification, including contradictions and temporal distortions that sentence-level scoring can obscure.

title: Optimizing Decomposition for Optimal Claim Verification
abstract: Studies how claim decomposition affects downstream verification and proposes dynamically adapting decomposition using verifier feedback rather than assuming a fixed notion of atomicity.

title: Decomposition Dilemmas: Does Claim Decomposition Boost or Burden Fact-Checking Performance?
abstract: Analyzes when decompose-then-verify pipelines help or hurt fact checking, including decomposition errors and the trade-off between simpler subclaims and loss or distortion of information.

title: Complex Claim Verification with Evidence Retrieved in the Wild
abstract: Builds a complex-claim verification pipeline combining claim decomposition, web retrieval, fine-grained evidence selection, evidence summarization, and final veracity prediction, while examining incompleteness in retrieved evidence.

title: A Claim Decomposition Benchmark for Long-Form Answer Verification
abstract: Introduces a benchmark for decomposing long-form answers into atomic claims suitable for independent verification, enabling evaluation below the sentence level.

title: FACTS&EVIDENCE: An Interactive Tool for Transparent Fine-Grained Factual Verification of Machine-Generated Text
abstract: Provides interactive fine-grained verification by breaking generated text into claims, retrieving multiple evidence sources, and exposing evidence and explanations so users can inspect attribution and support.

title: ToE: A Hierarchical and Explainable Claim Verification Framework with Dynamic Multi-source Evidence Retrieval and Aggregation
abstract: Uses a hierarchical argument tree with iterative decomposition, dynamic multi-source retrieval, evidence evaluation, aggregation, and verification to handle complex claims requiring evidence from multiple sources.

title: Fact Checking with Insufficient Evidence
abstract: Studies whether available evidence is sufficient for fact verification and develops diagnostics based on removing evidence constituents or sentences, separating evidence sufficiency from the final veracity decision.
venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics

title: RealRoute: Dynamic Query Routing System via Retrieve-then-Verify Paradigm
abstract: Proposes source-agnostic parallel retrieval followed by verification and dynamic routing across heterogeneous information sources, targeting evidence completeness and multi-hop questions rather than relying on one retrieval pass.

title: Evidence-Based Temporal Fact Verification
abstract: Develops an end-to-end temporal fact-verification approach that models events and time-sensitive evidence so claim validity can be assessed with respect to temporal context rather than as a timeless fact.

title: TSVer: A Benchmark for Fact Verification Against Time-Series Evidence
abstract: Introduces a benchmark in which real-world claims must be verified against time-series evidence, with annotations covering relevant time frames, verdicts, and justifications.

title: Towards Understanding Omission in Dialogue Summarization
abstract: Introduces explicit omission annotations and an omission-detection task for dialogue summaries, evaluating which important source information is absent from generated summaries rather than only measuring overall similarity or faithfulness.

title: Detecting Omissions in LLM-Generated Medical Summaries
abstract: Studies detection of clinically important information omitted from LLM-generated medical summaries and proposes a reference-free method for identifying such omissions.

title: Mitigating Hallucinations in Healthcare LLMs with Granular Fact-Checking and Domain-Specific Adaptation
abstract: Uses granular proposition mapping and checks for negation, implication, temporal, numerical, and semantic consistency against clinical records, together with presence checks intended to expose omitted information.

title: Unsupervised update summarization of news events
abstract: Presents unsupervised incremental summarization for evolving events, emphasizing novelty, cohesion, and information updates so later summaries avoid simply repeating earlier material.

title: Mining Sequential Update Summarization with Hierarchical Text Analysis
abstract: Addresses sequential update summarization for evolving information streams using hierarchical text analysis and evaluates update quality with temporal-summarization measures including comprehensiveness and latency-sensitive gain.

title: The Information Extraction Systems of PRIS at Temporal Summarization Track
abstract: Describes systems for the TREC Temporal Summarization tasks, including sequential update summarization and value tracking of attributes whose reported values can change over time.

title: CLIN-SUMM: Incremental Longitudinal Summarization of Clinical Notes Enables Scalable Representation and Early Disease Prediction
abstract: Constructs longitudinal patient representations incrementally, summarizing newly documented information at each encounter while preserving temporal ordering and avoiding future information leakage.

title: Selective Question Answering under Domain Shift
abstract: Studies selective question answering when deployment mixes in-domain and shifted examples, using a calibrator to decide which answers to return and evaluating error as coverage changes.

title: The Art of Abstention: Selective Prediction and Error Regularization for Natural Language Processing
abstract: Studies selective prediction for NLP, compares confidence estimators used for abstention, and introduces error regularization to improve the relationship between retained coverage and prediction risk.

title: Selective Classification for Deep Neural Networks
abstract: Develops selective classifiers for deep networks that can reject predictions to meet a desired risk level with high probability and evaluates performance through the risk-coverage trade-off.

title: SelectiveNet: A Deep Neural Network with an Integrated Reject Option
abstract: Introduces an end-to-end neural architecture that jointly learns prediction and selection, directly optimizing performance at a target coverage rather than adding rejection only after training.

title: Classification Methods with Reject Option Based on Convex Risk Minimization
abstract: Develops binary classification with a reject option using convex surrogate risks and establishes consistency and excess-risk results for decision rules that may abstain when classification is insufficiently reliable.

title: Optimal Strategies for Reject Option Classifiers
abstract: Provides a unified treatment of reject-option classification under cost-based, bounded-improvement, and bounded-abstention formulations, including optimal strategies connecting selective risk and achievable coverage.

title: Selective Classification Under Distribution Shifts
abstract: Studies selective classification under label, covariate, and out-of-distribution shifts and evaluates confidence scores and rejection strategies when test distributions differ from training.

title: Selective classification under imbalance in multiclass settings: A novel metric for bias-aware risk–coverage evaluation
abstract: Shows that aggregate risk-coverage evaluation can hide class-specific failures under imbalance and proposes class-aware measures and class-conditional rejection analysis.

title: Conformal selective prediction with cost aware deferral for safe clinical triage under distribution shift
abstract: Combines calibrated probabilistic prediction, conformal uncertainty sets, and cost-aware deferral, evaluating selective decisions and risk-coverage behavior on temporally separated in- and out-of-distribution clinical data.

title: COIN: Uncertainty-Guarding Selective Question Answering for Foundation Models with Provable Risk Guarantees
abstract: Develops uncertainty-aware selective question answering with statistical risk guarantees, using conformal techniques to control errors among answers that a foundation model elects to provide.

title: Conformal Inference for Online Prediction with Arbitrary Distribution Shifts
abstract: Develops online conformal inference for sequences whose distributions may vary arbitrarily, using adaptive procedures and regret-style guarantees to respond to non-stationarity rather than assuming a fixed exchangeable stream.

title: Conformal Risk Control
abstract: Generalizes conformal methods from set coverage to control of expected monotone loss, with extensions addressing distribution shift and other risk functions relevant to selective deployment.

title: Score-Based Diffusion Priors for Adaptive Conformal Inference under Distribution Shift
abstract: Combines adaptive conformal inference with score-based diffusion priors and online recalibration to improve coverage behavior under temporal and covariate distribution shifts.

title: Beyond conformal predictors: Adaptive Conformal Inference with confidence predictors
abstract: Studies adaptive conformal inference in non-exchangeable settings and incorporates confidence predictors to adapt uncertainty estimates as the data distribution changes.

title: Conformal prediction for labelling and updating online models in the presence of concept drift in cybersecurity
abstract: Investigates conformal prediction as a mechanism for assigning labels and updating online models under concept drift, directly testing recalibration and model adaptation in a changing data stream.
venue: Journal of Information Security and Applications

title: Language Models (Mostly) Know What They Know
abstract: Evaluates whether language models can estimate the probability that their own answers are correct, including explicit probability-of-correctness and probability-of-knowing judgments on question-answering tasks.

title: Semantic Uncertainty: Linguistic Invariances for Uncertainty Estimation in Natural Language Generation
abstract: Introduces semantic entropy, which aggregates probability across semantically equivalent generations to estimate task-level uncertainty and predict whether free-form answers are likely to be correct.

title: Can LLMs Express Their Uncertainty? An Empirical Evaluation of Confidence Elicitation in LLMs
abstract: Systematically evaluates methods for eliciting confidence from large language models, including verbalized confidence and sampling-based aggregation, and compares how well these estimates track answer correctness.

title: VERIFICATION OF FORECASTS EXPRESSED IN TERMS OF PROBABILITY
On optimum recognition error and reject tradeoff
abstract: Characterizes the trade-off between recognition error and rejection and derives an optimal rejection rule, providing a foundational decision-theoretic basis for selective prediction.

title: Humans or LLMs as the Judge? A Study on Judgement Biases
abstract: Compares human and LLM evaluators and investigates systematic judgment biases, showing that automatic judges can exhibit preferences unrelated to the intended evaluation construct.

title: Judging the Judges: A Systematic Study of Position Bias in LLM-as-a-Judge
abstract: Systematically measures position bias in LLM judges and examines repetition stability, consistency, and fairness, demonstrating that evaluator outputs can depend on presentation order.

title: Go-Figure: A Meta Evaluation of Factuality in Summarization
abstract: Meta-evaluates factuality metrics using controlled diagnostic data and human judgments, testing whether automatic measures behave correctly under different factual-error conditions rather than relying on benchmark correlation alone.

title: Are Factuality Checkers Reliable? Adversarial Meta-evaluation of Factuality in Summarization
abstract: Performs adversarial meta-evaluation of summarization factuality checkers on diagnostic datasets designed to expose specific weaknesses, showing that aggregate metric performance can hide systematic failure modes.

title: A Critical Look at Meta-evaluating Summarisation Evaluation Metrics
abstract: Critiques common meta-evaluation practice for summarization metrics, including narrow datasets and dimensions, and argues for more diverse, user-centered validation rather than treating a single correlation result as sufficient evidence.

title: Judging the Judges: Evaluating Alignment and Vulnerabilities in LLMs-as-Judges
abstract: Evaluates LLM judges against human judgments and analyzes vulnerabilities such as prompt sensitivity and leniency, emphasizing that raw agreement alone is insufficient to establish evaluator validity.

title: Judge's Verdict: A Comprehensive Analysis of LLM Judge Capability Through Human Agreement
abstract: Benchmarks LLM judging against human evaluation and examines agreement using measures beyond simple correlation, including reliability-oriented analyses intended to distinguish apparent scoring similarity from human-like judgment behavior.
